title: A circuit of positive depth is a gate
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit whose depth is at least $1$. Then $c$ is not a literal: it is an internal gate, so there exist a Boolean flag $\mathit{isAnd}$ and a list $cs$ of child circuits for which $c$ is the node with gate type $\mathit{isAnd}$ applied to the children $cs$.
hypotheses_covered: the depth of c is at least 1
replaced:
A circuit $c$ with $\mathrm{depth}\,c \geq 1$ is not a literal: there exist a Boolean
flag $\mathit{isAnd}$ and a child list $cs$ with $c = \mathrm{Circuit.node}\,\mathit{isAnd}\,cs$.
